# CAN log parsing fails with R/T flags in candump format

When parsing candump log files that include the R (remote) or T (transmit) flags at the end of the line, the parser fails to correctly extract the data.

## Description

The regular expression pattern used to parse candump log files doesn't properly handle the R/T flags that can appear at the end of candump lines. This affects both the logreader module and the plot functionality.

## Reproduction

Using a candump log file with R/T flags:

```
(1594172461.968006) vcan0 0C8#F000000000000000 T
(1594172463.968006) vcan0 0C8#F000000000000000 R
```

When trying to parse these lines, the data extraction fails because the regex pattern doesn't account for the trailing flags.

Similarly, when trying to plot data from a log file with these flags:

```
(1609395080.446193) vcan0 00000343#B504CB04AE04BC04 R
(1609395081.447989) vcan0 00000343#650457045E047404 R
(1609395082.449807) vcan0 00000343#1504240415043204 T
```

The plotting functionality doesn't correctly handle the data.

actions.new_string:
# Matches 'candump -l' (or -L) output, i.e. "(1594172461.968006) vcan0 1F0#0000000000001BC1"
# Also handles R/T flags, i.e. "(1594172461.968006) vcan0 0C8#F000000000000000 T"
RE_CANDUMP_LOG = re.compile(r'^\((?P<time>\d+\.\d+)\)\s+\S+\s+(?P<frameid>[\dA-F]+)#(?P<data>[\dA-F]*)(?:\s+[RT])?$')
